units.source_text: 女人回来后，一声不吭地在屋子角落里铺床。

en.t: After the woman came back, she spread out the bedding in the corner of the room without saying a word.

units.source_text: 这里让我睡了，她自己究竟要到哪里去睡呢？

en.t: If she let me sleep here, where on earth was she going to sleep herself?

units.source_text: 当然，帘子的那边有里屋。

en.t: Of course, there was an inner room beyond the curtain.

units.source_text: 其他地方也没见有像样的房间。

en.t: There did not seem to be any proper room anywhere else either.

units.source_text: 可是，主人睡里屋，却让客官睡大门口的屋子，这种做法可真让人无法理解。

en.t: But for the host to sleep in the inner room while making the guest sleep in the room by the entrance was truly impossible to understand.

units.source_text: 说不定，里屋有一个动弹不得的重病人躺着呢？

en.t: Could it be that a gravely ill person, unable to move, was lying in the inner room?

units.source_text: 真的，还是这样考虑来得自然。

en.t: Really, thinking of it that way seemed the most natural.

units.source_text: 首先，一个女人家不可能特地来接待一个萍水相逢的男客官。

en.t: To begin with, a woman living alone would hardly go out of her way to receive a male guest she had met only by chance.
